messages:
tess: Just opened a PR to add Hong Kong + Seoul to the Regions & Data Processing page and a short Dedicated migration checklist. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1002
omar: Thanks! Legal asked to replace 'data residency' with 'data processing region' everywhere and avoid saying data 'never leaves' a region. Please add an export-control footnote.
tess: Done in the PR description. Also added a footnote linking to the compliance page and the internal export-control doc.
rebecca: I'll add tiny SDK examples (py + ts) for choosing region and specifying a KMS key. planning to include a CLI snippet for migrations.
legal: Quick review Prefer phrasing: "Customer data is processed and stored in the selected region unless cross-region features are enabled or unless required by regulatory obligations." That should be included in the intro.
tess: updated intro with legal's sentence. Also changed table header to "Supported regions (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)" and added a footnote for Private availability being "by arrangement" in some APAC locations.
rebecca: pushed SDK commit with this Python sample:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(region="asia-east2", kms_key="projects/proj/locations/asia-east2/key1")
```
and a CLI migration dry-run:
```bash
redwoodctl migrate --customer 12345 --from us-east-1 --to eu-west-1 --dry-run
```
docs-bot: PR #1002 preview: https://docs-staging.redwood.ai/regions/1002  build OK
tess: QA ask: scan staging for absolutes like "never" or "guarantee" and comment inline. Legal will block otherwise.
omar: skimmed staging; left two inline comments to soften language and a note to use 'data processing region' consistently.
rebecca: added a troubleshooting blurb for "region mismatch" errors and a screenshot link of the Console region selector.
legal: +1 on wording after small tweak to the export-control footnote. Please don't use 'residency guarantee'.
tess: thanks all. merging once CI finishes and I'll add a one-line changelog to the docs digest. :white_check_mark:
